plants.name: Syringa vulgaris
plants.description: A deciduous shrub with dense, conical clusters of intensely fragrant flowers. It thrives in cold-winter climates and is a beloved garden staple, often planted near homes for its perfume.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late spring (late April to early June in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to the Balkan Peninsula; widely cultivated across temperate North America, Europe, and Asia
plants.funFact: Lilacs can live for more than 100 years, and old shrubs often persist at abandoned homesteads long after the buildings are gone.

plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: A herbaceous perennial producing large, showy, often double blooms with a sweet fragrance. It emerges in early spring and flowers in late spring, forming long-lived clumps in gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (May to June)
plants.location: Native to Siberia, Mongolia, and northern China; cultivated throughout temperate regions worldwide
plants.funFact: Peonies are the national flower of China in many traditions and can live and bloom for over 50 years in the same spot.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A tall subtropical tree covered in clouds of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers, often before the fern-like leaves fully emerge. In late spring it carpets streets with fallen blossoms in warm-climate cities of the Northern Hemisphere.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (May to June in the Northern Hemisphere; October to November in the Southern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in Mexico, California, Florida, the Mediterranean, and South Africa
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, tens of thousands of jacarandas earned it the nickname 'Jacaranda City,' while Mexico City and Lisbon also have famous displays around this time.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: An evergreen shrub that flowers in the cool months of the Southern Hemisphere. Its delicate, often fragrant flowers appear against glossy dark green leaves as autumn deepens toward winter.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn to early winter (April to July in the Southern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to Japan; cultivated in Australia, New Zealand, South Africa, and southern Chile
plants.funFact: Camellia sinensis, a close relative, is the plant that produces all true tea, while sasanqua seeds are pressed for a culinary and cosmetic oil.
